items.title: An Innovative EEG-Based Pain Identification and Quantification: A Pilot Study
items.authors: Colince Meli Segning, Rubens A. da Silva, Suzy Ngomo
items.feature_definition: Authors band-pass beta at 13–30 Hz, form Hilbert analytic signal, take upper-envelope magnitude, and compute SD/mean × 100%; normalization references the first 60 s.
items.prediction_rationale: Authors propose envelope variability as a scale-independent cue for pain presence/magnitude; it is an exploratory association, not a held-out predictor.
items.verified_result_metric: In chronic-pain Group 3 (n=66), source reports Piqβ–VNRS r=0.69, p<0.0001 and R²=0.47; the source does not establish externally validated prediction. Authors visually propose Piqβ≥10% as a pain threshold.
items.prediction_target: Pain presence and participant-reported pain intensity (VNRS).
items.validation_design: Pilot convenience samples: 7 capsaicin, 15 thermal-pain and 66 chronic-pain participants; 5-min EEG; threshold proposed from observed groups, with no independent test set or external validation.
items.open_access_status: Freely readable full text in PMC; CC BY article.
items.data_url: Not public; article reports data cannot be publicly shared owing to confidentiality and an ongoing patent application.
items.data_evidence: Saved source excerpt states raw data cannot be publicly shared for confidentiality and ongoing patent application; no public EEG repository is linked. Not eligible as a public-EEG validation item.
items.relevance_limitations: 10% is a pilot threshold, not universal reliability/sensitivity; channels FC5/T7 are absent from C3/C4/Cz; 30–43 Hz gamma fits current 1–40 Hz only partly and is not evidence about >64 Hz high gamma; baseline/task timing and 60-s reference differ from generic 5-s windows.

items.title: Towards the Objective Identification of the Presence of Pain Based on Electroencephalography Signals’ Analysis: A Proof-of-Concept
items.feature_family: CVUE in alpha, beta and gamma; beta upper-envelope variability emphasized
items.feature_definition: Hilbert upper-envelope coefficient of variation from FC5 and T7; alpha 8–12, beta 12–30 and gamma 30–43 Hz; compared at rest and during a visuo-motor task.
items.prediction_rationale: Authors propose increased CVUEβ at FC5 as an indicator of pain presence; no supervised predictive model is established.
items.verified_result_metric: Abstract reports CVUEβ increased up to 20% at rest in pain conditions and reports no correlation with pain intensity or task performance; n=4 chronic fibromyalgia and n=7 experimentally induced pain/control participants.
items.prediction_target: Pain presence; pain intensity and task performance were also assessed.
items.validation_design: Small proof-of-concept, group contrasts with baseline/rest and active-task conditions; no independent test cohort.
items.open_access_status: Freely readable full text in PMC; open-access Sensors article.
items.data_url: No public EEG repository identified in the inspected paper/source pages.
items.data_evidence: The inspected article provides no verified public raw-EEG repository link; do not treat accessible tables/figures as raw EEG.
items.relevance_limitations: Does not validate a universal 10% reliability threshold; n is very small, no intensity correlation, and FC5/T7 are not available in the C3/C4/Cz pipeline. Its task/rest comparisons require timing and baseline distinctions.

items.title: Neural variability reliably encodes interindividual differences in the perception of pain intensity
items.authors: Li-Bo Zhang, Xin-Yi Geng, Li Hu et al.
items.feature_family: Temporal response standard deviation and permutation entropy (PE)
items.feature_definition: Temporal SD of evoked EEG responses in 100-ms sliding windows; PE compares ordinal pattern probabilities. Paper analyzes six datasets (total N=633) and describes a Cz time point analysis.
items.prediction_rationale: Authors interpret variability as encoding individual differences in pain-intensity discriminability; association does not equal an evaluated prediction model.
items.verified_result_metric: Dataset 1 ROI near the variability peak: r=0.43, p=1.16×10⁻⁷, BF=8.05×10⁴ for temporal-SD difference vs pain-rating difference; partial r≈0.45, p=2.23×10⁻⁸ controlling for amplitude. PE associations are reported, but no theta-specific weighted-feature claim is verified.
items.prediction_target: Between-person pain-intensity discriminability (high-minus-low subjective rating), not trial-level pain rating prediction.
items.validation_design: Retrospective analysis of six datasets, with replicability across multiple datasets and amplitude/noise control analyses; correlation analyses, not held-out classifier/regressor validation.
items.open_access_status: Freely readable full text in PMC; PLOS Biology open access.
items.data_evidence: Article links figure-underlying data to OSF DOI; OSF landing page confirms a public project, but raw EEG files were not verified there. Do not label as public raw EEG.
items.relevance_limitations: The primary metric is event-locked ERP variability in 100-ms windows, not generic 5-s resting variance; needs stimulus timing/baseline and event-epoch support. Cz is pipeline-compatible, but full method cannot be reproduced from figure data alone.

items.title: Markers of Central Neuropathic Pain in Higuchi Fractal Analysis of EEG Signals From People With Spinal Cord Injury
items.authors: Keri Anderson, Cristian Chirion, Matthew Fraser, Mariel Purcell, Sebastian Stein, Aleksandra Vuckovic
items.feature_definition: Non-oscillatory HFD computed from EEG during imagined movement; the study tests group differences and machine-learning classification in chronic/subacute spinal-cord-injury pain cohorts.
items.prediction_rationale: Authors investigate HFD as a prognostic/diagnostic feature for central neuropathic pain after SCI; their interpretation is not general nociceptive pain-intensity prediction.
items.verified_result_metric: Abstract reports transferable classifiers with >80% accuracy for chronic-SCI groups using a single EEG channel; HFD differs across chronic and 6-month follow-up groups. Metric is classification accuracy, not variance explained or pain-intensity correlation.
items.prediction_target: Chronic central neuropathic pain group status and later CNP development after SCI.
items.validation_design: Two datasets: chronic groups (10 able-bodied, 10 SCI+CNP, 10 SCI without CNP) and subacute SCI follow-up (N=20; 10 developed CNP); bootstrapped group tests and transferable classifier. Raw dataset availability not verified.
items.open_access_status: Freely readable full text in PMC; Frontiers open-access article.
items.data_url: No linked public raw EEG repository verified.
items.data_evidence: Paper describes existing EEG datasets but this research pass did not verify a public repository tied to them; candidate only for public-data criterion.
items.relevance_limitations: Frontal effects/channels and imagined-movement epochs may be essential; frontal sensors are absent from C3/C4/Cz and movement event timing is not represented by generic 5-s windows. Clinical SCI neuropathic pain is not equivalent to acute pain-intensity rating.

items.title: A comprehensive EEG dataset of laser-evoked potentials for pain research
items.feature_family: Raw evoked EEG suitable for derived amplitude/variance/entropy feature comparisons; descriptor does not itself validate these features.
items.feature_definition: Nine OpenNeuro BIDS laser-evoked EEG experiments with trial intensity and subjective pain ratings; paper states raw EEG files and per-trial labels are available.
items.prediction_rationale: Candidate public benchmark for testing proposed amplitude-envelope variance, SD, entropy or HFD against stimulus intensity and single-trial pain ratings; this is a proposed reuse, not the paper's reported model.
items.verified_result_metric: Not a prediction paper. Descriptor reports LEP response increases with laser stimulus intensity and a similar relation to subjective ratings; no feature-family prediction metric verified.
items.prediction_target: Trial-level reported pain rating / stimulus intensity, for proposed feature evaluation.
items.validation_design: Data descriptor combines nine experiments and 678 healthy participants; no model validation design reported. OpenNeuro confirms BIDS EEG and pain-rating task files in ds005284 and ds005473.
items.open_access_status: Freely readable full text in PMC / Scientific Data.
items.data_url: https://openneuro.org/datasets/ds005284/versions/1.0.0 (paper additionally lists ds005285, ds005289, ds005286, ds005291, ds005293, ds005292, ds005280 and ds005473).
items.data_evidence: Paper explicitly maps its nine experiments to OpenNeuro dataset DOIs, identifies subject-level raw .eeg/.bdf files and per-trial ratings; OpenNeuro pages fetched for ds005284 and ds005473 show EEG modality, downloadable BIDS files and laser pain rating instructions.
items.relevance_limitations: Event-locked, high-density and heterogeneous acquisition; use event labels/baselines and appropriate channel mapping rather than unaligned five-second segments. No source validation of CVUE, Hjorth, entropy, HFD or >64-Hz features.

items.title: PhysioPain Dataset
items.authors: Boran Toktay, İkbal Işık Orhan, Elif Yıldırım, Fatma Patlar Akbulut et al.
items.feature_family: Pain-labelled EEG-derived bands (not verified raw voltage EEG)
items.feature_definition: Dataset contains pain questionnaire and EEG device outputs; paper describes MindWave brainwave bands sampled at 1 Hz and stored processed EEG by pain label/intensity. This supports only reanalysis of stored derived data, not recomputation of CVUE/HFD/entropy on raw samples.
items.prediction_rationale: Potential baseline for pain-type/intensity classification using its published derived EEG-band series; raw-signal nonlinear-feature analysis is not supported by verified files.
items.verified_result_metric: Dataset paper reports no validated prediction metric; data resource only.
items.prediction_target: Pain type/intensity self-report (headache, back/neck/waist, menstrual, no-pain labels).
items.validation_design: 99 collected; paper says 6 excluded from core analytical cohort (n=93). Dataset page offers public download; no prediction validation design for this resource.
items.open_access_status: Freely readable full text in PMC / Data in Brief.
items.data_evidence: Paper links its PhysioPain original-data record and a table identifies Mendeley DOI 10.17632/mf2cgph9cy.4; fetched Mendeley page offers a 1.16-GB CC BY 4.0 download and describes 99 participants, survey answers and raw/processed device exports. Paper characterizes EEG as 1-Hz MindWave band outputs, not verified continuous raw voltage.
items.relevance_limitations: 1-Hz derived band streams cannot reproduce beta-envelope CV, HFD or entropy on EEG waveform; likely unsuitable for event-level five-second EEG features. Do not overstate as public raw EEG.

items.title: Electroencephalography Signatures for Conditioned Pain Modulation and Pain Perception in Nonspecific Chronic Low Back Pain—An Exploratory Study
items.authors: Paulo E. P. Teixeira et al.
items.feature_family: EEG spectral signal strength (relative power), not CVUE/nonlinear complexity
items.feature_definition: Resting-state absolute/relative delta–beta power per electrode, using 5-s FFT windows with 50% overlap; 30-patient cross-sectional chronic low-back-pain sample.
items.prediction_rationale: Authors report central delta/theta relative power associations with self-reported pain when controlling for depression; transferable baseline signal-strength features, not a validated predictor.
items.verified_result_metric: Authors say significant delta/theta EEG models explained approximately 20% of pain-score variability; separate CPM–pain model R²=0.12 and nonsignificant (p=.12). The EEG result is exploratory, not held-out accuracy.
items.prediction_target: Seven-day average self-reported low-back-pain VAS; CPM was a separate target.
items.validation_design: N=30 cross-sectional exploratory regressions with feature screening/backward selection; no external test set. EEG model includes mood/QST covariates.
items.open_access_status: Freely readable full text in PMC.
items.data_url: No linked public EEG repository verified.
items.data_evidence: Inspected full-text excerpt documents study and results but no verified linked public raw-EEG repository; source tables are not raw EEG.
items.relevance_limitations: 5-s windows and 1–40 Hz match the current pipeline; central channels include C3/C4/Cz, but paper also uses frontal/parietal sensors unavailable here. Tests relative power, not variance/CVUE/HFD/PE; no public raw data verified.

items.title: Pain and the Brain: A Systematic Review of Methods, EEG Biomarkers, Limitations, and Future Directions
items.feature_family: Review coverage includes spectral entropy, permutation entropy and multiscale sample entropy among pain-EEG methods.
items.feature_definition: Narrative/systematic literature synthesis; no new EEG signal feature or dataset is produced.
items.prediction_rationale: Useful map of candidate feature families and limitations; not evidence that any entropy is a validated pain predictor or top-weighted feature.
items.verified_result_metric: Not applicable to the review as a new prediction model; reviewed study metrics were not independently recoded in this pass.
items.prediction_target: Not applicable; review-level coverage of pain EEG methods.
items.open_access_status: Freely readable full text in PMC; open-access Neurology International review.
items.data_evidence: Review article; no new participant EEG dataset.
items.relevance_limitations: Review-level categorization is not primary evidence of feature performance; exact statement that theta permutation entropy is the highest weighted feature was not verified.

conflicts: CVUE/Piqβ ≥10% is a source-proposed pilot threshold, not verified reliability: the 2022 proof-of-concept has n=4 chronic-pain and n=7 induced-pain/control participants, reports no CVUEβ–pain-intensity correlation, and lacks external validation; the 2024 pilot reports a chronic-group association but its raw data are not public. Neither source establishes universal sensitivity/specificity or test–retest reliability.

The 2022 no-intensity-correlation result and 2024 r=.69 result have different samples/designs and should not be collapsed into one replicated effect. 2024 R²=.47 is a source-reported within-sample relationship, not held-out model performance.

Theta permutation entropy as the highest weighted feature was not verified. The 2025 variability paper analyzes PE and temporal SD, reporting pain-discriminability correlations; no theta band, feature-weight ranking or classification weighting claim was found in the primary evidence inspected.

PhysioPain is openly downloadable and linked by its data paper, but its EEG exports are described as 1-Hz MindWave band data; this is not verified raw voltage EEG for computing CVUE/Hjorth/HFD/entropy. PainMonit was screened out because the cited dataset modalities do not include EEG.
gaps: This verified pass yields a small set of relevant items, not 100; no padding or duplicate variants used. Only the laser-evoked OpenNeuro resource was verified here as public raw EEG with pain-linked single-trial ratings.
No publicly shared raw EEG was verified for either CVUE/Piqβ paper, and the 10% threshold needs independent calibration, reliability testing, sensitivity/specificity and external validation.
No pain-specific Hjorth study or sample-entropy prediction with public raw EEG was verified in this pass; theta-weighted permutation-entropy assertion remains unsubstantiated.

Pipeline channel limits exclude CVUE papers' FC5/T7/frontotemporal locations; HFD SCI work emphasizes frontal regions and imagined movement. LEP and temporal-SD evidence requires event-locked stimulus/baseline timing; 100-ms variability windows do not match unaligned 5-s windows.

At 128 Hz, Nyquist is 64 Hz, so >64-Hz high-gamma content is not representable; the current 1–40-Hz filter excludes it regardless. None of the verified CVUE sources supports extrapolation to >64-Hz activity.

queries: Which peer-reviewed EEG pain studies quantify amplitude envelope variance, coefficient of variation, CVUE, or Piq beta and report reliability or pain prediction results?
What pain EEG studies use Hjorth parameters, permutation entropy, sample entropy, or Higuchi fractal dimension, and what open EEG data are linked to them?
Which EEG pain datasets are openly downloadable with paper-linked evidence, especially thermal pain, laser pain, or pain intensity ratings?
Which open-access EEG signal prediction and nonlinear feature papers report theta permutation entropy as a weighted feature or CVUE at least 10 percent reliability?
